messages:
emily: heads-up: onboarding run for quant3-14b-int3 with long-prefill (60k) produced a reproducible KV mismatch pattern that isn't a simple wrap/clip. opening thread so we can coordinate.

rahul: mismatch pattern? paste logs and invocation.

emily: invocation: 
```bash
./onboard.sh --model=quant3-14b-int3 --prefill=60000 --quant=int3 --trace=kv,evict
```
log excerpt: 
```
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] kv.write req=59988 stored=59988
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] kv.write req=60009 stored=60009
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] kv.evict shrink_to=58432 (prefix-evict triggered)
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] kv.write req=60021 stored=58433  # unexpected: new write landed at evicted slot
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] kv.read  req=60021 served=58433
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] rotary.apply pos=60021 used=58433
[2026-11-10T09:12:01Z] gen token="in" prob_delta=0.014
```

zoe: interesting: that looks like a race between prefix-eviction (freeing low slots) and a stale "head" pointer that maps new global_pos -> local_slot using (global_pos - base) without atomically updating base. if base moved but head didn't, new writes can land in recently evicted slots and appear as stale content.

rahul: iirc we optimized eviction path in the int3 kernel by doing a non-atomic base increment for perf (assumed single-writer). maybe a shim in the quant fast-path bypasses the mutex. searching.

emily: small repro harness that deterministically triggers: single-threaded, prefill until eviction threshold then burst-writes in same tick. attaching: 
```python
# kv_evict_race_repro.py
from runtime import Runner
r = Runner('quant3-14b-int3')
# simulate many small writes then a big prefill to trigger prefix-evict
r.prefill('A'*60000)
print(r.trace.kv_events[-10:])
```

zoe: mitigation options: 1) make prefix-evict update both base and head under lock (safe but perf cost), 2) make writers check base before writing and retry if base advanced (lockless retry), 3) enable kv.repair-scan on canary to detect and reject served_pos != req_pos during traces.

rahul: i'll prototype option 2 (write-then-verify-retry) in fast-path. should be a small patch: after computing slot = map(global_pos), check if base changed from snapshot -> if yes recompute slot. adds one extra read but avoids full mutex.

emily: can we enable kv.repair-scan on pool-canary-5 until patch lands? it will OOM for huge traces but for canary it's ok.

ops: enabled kv.repair-scan=true and kv.index.trace=256 on pool-canary-5. build-bot: starting CI for patch-1755555555.

build-bot: CI queued: quant3-int3/patch-1755555555. Unit tests: kv-evict-race, kv-index-consistency.

zoe: also adding a unit test that simulates interleaved evict+write bursts and asserts no served_pos < req_pos. will include in kernel tests and make it run in dev-only CI profile.

rahul: patch pushed (PR: /r/quant3/1755555555-evict-retry). adding debug-only metric kv.write.retries to monitor in canary.

emily: once patch lands let's run float32 vs int3 differential on longprefill goldset with same RNG to confirm quality gap closes. leaving traces on for 6 runs. :thumbsup:
